headline: Approved Gate City Casino at 11 Tara Boulevard with conditions, and a medical office building at 44 Simon Street.
summary: A proposed video display sign overlay on Main Street was unfavorably recommended to the Board of Aldermen, and an auction of tax-deeded property was favorably recommended with a request to further investigate two parcels. Gate City Casino at 11 Tara Boulevard was approved in two phases with conditions, and a site plan for a medical office building at 44 Simon Street was approved. Conditional use permits for 17 Marshall Street and 7 Haines Street and a subdivision at 57 Factory Street were also approved.
decisions: Unfavorably recommended the Video Display Signs Overlay District referral O-26-022 to the Board of Aldermen, 5-1-1, with Morgan opposed and Hudson abstaining.

Postponed the subdivision application A26-0103 for 28 Lincoln Avenue to the September 3, 2026 meeting.
Approved conditional use permit A26-0134 for a car care center at 17 Marshall Street, 6-0, with the condition that Engineering comments be resolved before the building permit is issued.
Approved the waivers requested for site plan A26-0133 at 44 Simon Street, 5-0.
Approved site plan A26-0133 for a 3-story medical office building at 44 Simon Street with conditions, including a $31,250 contribution to the West Hollis Traffic Mitigation Account, 5-0.
Approved conditional use permit A26-0013 for the Gate City Casino at 11 Tara Boulevard, 5-0.
Approved the waivers requested for site plan A26-0012 at 11 Tara Boulevard, 5-0.
Approved Phase I of site plan A26-0012 at 11 Tara Boulevard with conditions, 5-0.
Defined active and substantive development for the Tara Boulevard project, 5-0.
Approved Phase II of site plan A26-0012 at 11 Tara Boulevard with precedent and subsequent conditions, 5-0.
Approved conditional use permit A26-0112 for a 3-unit multi-family building at 7 Haines Street with conditions, 5-0.
Approved the waivers requested for subdivision plan A26-0109 at 57 Factory Street, 5-0.
Approved the 2-unit condominium subdivision A26-0109 at 57 Factory Street with conditions, 5-0.

EXPANDED DRAFT MEETING SUMMARY 
THIS IS NOT AN OFFICIAL TRANSCRIPT OF TAPE RECORDED PROCEEDINGS 
THE INFORMATION CONTAINED HEREIN HAS NOT BEEN REVIEWED OR APPROVED BY THE NCPB 
 
NASHUA CITY PLANNING BOARD 
August 6, 2026 
 
The regularly scheduled meeting of the Nashua City Planning Board 
was held on August 6, 2026 at 7:00PM in the 3 rd floor auditorium 
in City Hall. 
 
Members Present: Joe MacIntyre, Mayor’s Representative 
 Bob Bollinger, Chair 
 Adam Varley, Vice Chair 
 Cameron Green, Secretary 
 Dan Hudson, City Engineer 
 Ald. Amber Morgan 
 Scott LeClair (Alt.)  
  
Also Present: Sam Durfee, Planning Manager 
 Connor Muise, Deputy Planning Manager 
 Scott McPhie, Planner I 
  
APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
 
July 9, 2026 
 
MOTION by Mr. Varley to approve the minutes, as written 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Hudson 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
COMMUNICATIONS 
 
- A26-0112, 7 Haines St 
o Abutter correspondence  
o Updated site survey 
- A26-0109, 57 Factory St

o Updated plan 
- A26-0133, 44 Simon St 
o Updated staff report 
o Presentation materials 
- A26-0012 & A26-0013, 11 Tara Blvd 
o Traffic, property values, CUP criteria, etc.  
o Abutter correspondence 
 
REPORT OF CHAIR, COMMITTEE, & LIAISON 
 
None
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 2 
 
 
PROCEDURES OF THE MEETING 
 
After the legal notice of each conditional, special use permit, 
site plan or subdivision plan is read by the Chair, the Board will 
determine if that the application is complete and ready for the 
Board to take jurisdiction. The public hearing will begin at which 
time the applicant or representative will be given time to present 
an overview and description of their project. The applicant shall 
speak to whether or not they agree with recommended staff 
stipulations. The Board will then have an opportunity to ask 
questions of the applicant or staff. 
 
The Chair will then ask for testimony from the audience. First 
anyone wishing to speak in opposition or with concern to the plan 
may speak. Please come forward to the microphone, state their name 
and address for the record. This would be the time to ask questions 
they may have regarding the plan. Next public testimony will come 
from anyone wishing to speak in favor of the plan. The applicant 
will then be allowed a rebuttal period at which time they shall 
speak to any issues or concerns raised by prior public testimony. 
 
One public member will then be granted an opportunity to speak to 
those issues brought by the applicant during their rebuttal period. 
The Board will then ask any relevant follow-up questions of the 
applicant if need be. 
 
After this is completed the public hearing will end and the Board 
will resume the public meeting at which time the Board will 
deliberate and vote on the application before us. The Board asks 
that both sides keep their remarks to the subject at hand and try 
not to repeat what has already been said. 
 
Above all, the Board wants to be fair to everyone and make the 
best possible decision based on the testimony presented and all 
applicable approval criteria established in the Nashua Revised 
Ordinances for conditional, special use permits, site plans and 
subdivisions. Thank you for your interest and courteous attention. 
Please turn off your cell phones and pagers at this time. 
 
Per our legal charter, we have a quorum when five members are 
present. There may be some recusals this evening for certain board 
members, but as long as five members are sitting each case can be 
heard. At the discretion of the chair, the order of the cases can 
be rearranged.
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 3 
 
NEW BUSINESS – SUBDIVISION PLANS 
A26-0103  Kelly A. McAllister (Owner & Applicant) requesting 
approval for a 2-lot subdivision. Property is located at 
28 Lincoln Avenue. Map 9 – Lot 18. Zoned B-Urban 
Residence (RB). Ward 7. (Postponed to September 3, 2026 
meeting) 
OTHER BUSINESS 
 
1. Review of tentative agenda to determine proposals of regional 
impact. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Varley that there are no items of regional impact 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Green  
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
2. Board of Aldermen Referral O-26-022, Establishing the Video 
Display Signs Overlay District 
 
Sam Durfee, Planning Manager 
 
Mr. Durfee said this is a possible overlay district, bounded by 
the Nashua River to the north and East/West Hollis Streets to the 
south. This is applicable to all buildings and properties that 
have frontage on Main Street. This leans heavily on the dimensional 
standards for wall signs that already exist in the ordinance, and 
would allow for those wall signs to have video displays. This is 
a step above electronic messaging centers (EMC), no longer static 
text. This could have moving images. No audio, and there are some 
standards around ensuring that the images and frequency they change 
would not be distracting to drivers.  
 
Mr. Bollinger asked if there is a staff opinion on whether or not 
this comports with existing code or the upcoming recode effort.  
 
Mr. Durfee said it objectively does not comport with the existing 
code because this is an amendment. To reframe, does it further the 
goals and objectives of the Master Plan? He thinks it’s does. We 
are very pro economic development and this could be viewed as a 
vehicle for that. We have provisions where the sign could not cover 
up significant architectural features, we have a lot of old 
buildings in the downtown with distinct features.
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 4 
 
Mr. Varley asked if this would be unique in the city.  
 
Mr. Durfee said yes, we don’t have any provisions for moving signs.  
 
Mr. Varley asked what would be the process currently if any 
business wanted to use a sign of this type? Is it prohibited 
outright? 
 
Mr. Durfee said it would be a variance through the zoning board.  
 
Mr. Bollinger asked if there is a process right now.  
 
Mr. Durfee said there’s always a process.  
 
Mr. Varley said under base code it’s not permitted.  
 
Mr. Durfee said correct.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said he’s struggling. There’s already a mechanism by 
which someone could do this if they wanted to. He doesn’t want to 
give a blanket approval to every business on Main Street to have 
this type of sign. It seems like what this legislation would do.  
 
Mr. Durfee said his read of the applicability is correct. It is 
all the buildings fronting on Main Street between the river and 
East/West Hollis St. 
 
Mr. Bollinger said you accept a certain amount of that on other 
commercial corridors, he is struggling with it on Main Street.  
 
Mr. Green said when he thinks of premier downtown areas, he doesn’t 
think of billboards. It seems like an odd exception to have it on 
the entire corridor instead of a case by case basis.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre said this is endorsed by Board of Alderman President 
Wilshire. He would like to ask Ald. Morgan for clarification, has 
the Board of Aldermen discussed this? 
 
Ald. Morgan said no. This is the first discussion. The other 
committee is Planning and Economic Development. After those two it 
goes back to the Board of Alderman with either a favorable or 
unfavorable recommendation.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre asked if the Planning Board has a negative view of 
this, does this carry much significance?
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 5 
 
Mr. Bollinger said they will vote on it independent of this Board.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre said that’s not the intent of his question.  
 
Mr. Durfee said he’s not willing to prescribe weight to the Board’s 
opinions to the BOA. He thinks this is the greatest Board in the 
city, but that’s just his isolated opinion of the Planning Board. 
 
Ald. Morgan said the Planning Board’s opinion is heavily weighted. 
Each person is independent in their voting, but recommendations 
from other city boards carry a lot of weight.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre asked if there were historical data points on 
something like this. He senses that we don’t feel too good on this, 
what would happen if this is not recommended? 
 
Mr. Bollinger said in his opinion, he is having a moment of pause. 
It seems like a solution to a problem that doesn’t exist. As 
business friendly as Nashua is, he doesn’t see that inherently 
advancing that cause.  
 
Mr. LeClair said there have been several other ordinances that 
we’ve given comments on and seen changes go through, like the ADU 
ordinance. He’s definitely seen that happen on more than one 
occasion in his years here.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said the BOA listens but it’s nonbinding.  
 
Ald. Morgan asked if the 35-ft measurement in the ordinance is 
where the sign can start, or the maximum height of the sign.  
 
Mr. Durfee said it is an endpoint, there can be no signage higher 
than 35-ft as measured from the ground.  
 
Ald. Morgan asked if there is an opportunity to change that. She 
wouldn’t want to see signage on the third floor, second floor, or 
first floor.  
 
Mr. Durfee said that can be part of the motion.  
 
Mr. Varley said it’s not clear to him what the impetus for this 
ordinance and what need this is serving. He worries about providing 
a blanket approval in advance as opposed to a case by case review. 
 
Mr. Bollinger said if someone is willing to make a motion, they 
can work in Ald. Morgan’s comments on height.
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 6 
 
 
Mr. Varley said he is willing to make a motion, but it would be to 
unfavorably recommend.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said if that is the case, there can be reasons for 
denial. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Varley to unfavorably recommend O-26-022 to the Board 
of Aldermen 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Green 
 
Mr. MacIntyre said he is willing to go along with the Board because 
he feels the signal is clearer to the BOA if the Board is unanimous 
in its dissent. 
 
Mr. Bollinger said we are not bound to unanimous votes.  
 
Mr. LeClair said it would be worth stating a reason in the motion. 
That we don’t feel this is necessary because there is an existing 
procedure to get this done on a case by case basis.  
 
Mr. Varley said he will amend his motion.   
 
MOTION by Mr. Varley to unfavorably recommend O-26-022 to the Board 
of Aldermen, on the basis that the Planning Board does not believe 
a blanket approval is the best method for allowing this type of 
signage. Instead this should be handled on a case by case basis 
through the Zoning Board.  
 
SECONDED by Mr. Green 
 
Mr. Hudson said he will abstain from this, as he doesn’t live in 
the community. He feels that these community decisions about what 
people want in their downtown are not his place.  
 
MOTION CARRIED 5-1-1 (Morgan opposed, Hudson abstained) 
 
3. Board of Aldermen Referral R-26-051, Relative to Auctioning Tax 
Deeded Property. 
 
Sam Durfee, Planning Manager 
 
Mr. Durfee said this is largely driven by state statute. There are 
a number of properties conveyed to the city through delinquent tax 
bills. Going through the statutory process, we would be putting
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 7 
 
these out to auction. The Board has the ability to comment on these 
properties.  
 
Mr. Hudson said he has reviewed the list. L Hassell Brook Road has 
sewer lines cutting through in two locations, and drainage outlets 
that discharge to the property, so he doesn’t believe that’s a 
good property for the city to dispose of. The other one is L 
Narrows Road, it’s a landlocked parcel surrounded by conservation 
land. That one should be considered to be retained.  
 
Mr. Bollinger asked if that is beyond the airport.  
 
Mr. Hudson said yes.  
 
MOTION by Mr. Varley to favorably recommend R-26-051, with the 
recommendation to further investigate L Hassel Road & L Narrows 
parcels to confirm whether they are appropriate to sell 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Green 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
NEW BUSINESS – CONDITIONAL USE APPLICATIONS 
A26-0134  17 Marshall, LLC / D Lines Auto Spot, LLC (Owner / 
Applicant) requesting conditional use approval for a car 
care center. Property is located at 17 Marshall Street. 
Map 29 – Lot 48. Zoned General Industrial (GI). Ward 7. 
MOTION by Mr. Green that the application is complete and the 
Planning Board is ready to take jurisdiction 
 
SECONDED by Mr. LeClair 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green that A26-0134 is not a development of regional 
impact 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Hudson 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
Kevin Corriveau, Owner, 17 Marshall St, Nashua NH 
 
Mr. Corriveau said this is a conditional use permit for his tenant, 
to operate a car detailing business.
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 8 
 
 
Mr. Bollinger asked for a brief overview of what is proposed and 
the approval criteria.  
 
Mr. Corriveau said this is a car detailing business, window tinting 
and so forth. He listed the nine criteria of the conditional use 
permit and how this business meets the requirements.   
 
Mr. Bollinger asked if they had an opportunity to review staff 
comments and the Engineering letter.  
 
Mr. Corriveau said no.  
 
Mr. Hudson summarized the July 30, 2026 letter. He asked if the 
applicant would have to return to the Board if they expanded to 
other car care like repair work.  
 
Mr. Durfee asked if he is concerned about oil spills. 
 
Mr. Hudson said yes, and traffic related issues. If turned into a 
car wash that would be a different situation.   
 
Mr. Durfee said that would be a change of use, which would 
necessitate going through the administrative review process. In 
that case, we would have the opportunity to review it. It is still 
under the conditional use permit criteria.  
 
Mr. Hudson said he is satisfied that there is a mechanism.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said the applicant should reach out to Engineering 
to provide the information requested. It’s nothing that we wouldn’t 
ask for on a similar type of application. Is there a set hour of 
operation? 
 
Unknown, Applicant 
 
Mr. [Applicant] said 8AM-8PM.  
 
Ald. Morgan said in her past life she was a manager for a custom 
car shop in Vegas. Will there be any auto lifts? 
 
Mr. [Applicant] said no, absolutely not.  
 
Mr. Corriveau said nothing mechanical in there.
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 9 
 
Mr. Hudson provided the applicant with a copy of the Engineering 
letter.  
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR CONCERN 
 
Gary Sinclair, 19 Marshall St, Nashua NH 
 
Mr. Sinclair said he doesn’t think this should be approved. There 
is way too much traffic. The owner parks his trailers and trucks 
on my property and I have to confront him about it, he blames it 
on the subcontractor. It’s a constant thing. He doesn’t have any 
more land to do this, with the traffic he already has from his 
painting business. The other thing is snow removal, the owner 
already pushes snow right up against my building and buries my gas 
meter. There’s no place to put the snow, there’s no place to put 
anything. This will bring in more cars, where are you going to put 
everything? This shouldn’t be passed.  
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR 
 
None 
 
APPLICANT REBUTTAL 
 
Kevin Corriveau, Owner 
 
Mr. Corriveau said he feels he has already addressed traffic. 
Across the street is 22 Marshall St, there is a 152-unit 
development. He built his business when there was nothing across 
the street. He rented a building from Mr. Sinclair. Mr. Sinclair 
has an HVAC business in his building, those trucks pull into my 
driveway and cut across into his property to park. He thinks it is 
ironic that Mr. Sinclair is here in opposition, in 2019 he rented 
to a car detailing business. He never received a notice from the 
Planning Board, his abutter didn’t go through the proper channels.  
 
PUBLIC MEETING 
 
Mr. Bollinger closed the public hearing and opened the public 
meeting. He feels the applicant has satisfied the criteria. There’s 
a little cleanup work to do with Engineering, but that’s not 
uncommon. In regards to the parking and neighbor disputes, it looks 
like there are at least 8 parking spots onsite plus the bays that 
could be utilized. He feels that would be sufficient to accommodate 
this. He cannot address issues regarding snow. This Board is
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 10 
 
charged with determining whether the business has satisfied the 
criteria.  
 
Mr. Green said one of the criteria requires addressing Mr. 
Mendola’s engineering letter, which references traffic. That has 
to be satisfied before they can have this use. 
 
Mr. MacIntyre said he toured the area and does not feel it would 
be an issue. This fits the Master Plan in encouraging small 
businesses. He hopes they can solve their neighborly problems, but 
other than that it looks good.  
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve New Business – Conditional Use 
Permit A26-0134. The Board finds that the application meets the 
Approval Criteria under §190-134(F) with the following conditions: 
 
1. Prior to issuing the building permit, all comments in the memo 
from Joe Mendola, Senior Staff Engineer, dated July 30, 2026 
will be resolved to the satisfaction of the Division of Public 
Works. 
 
SECONDED by Ald. Morgan 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0 
 
NEW BUSINESS – SITE PLANS 
A26-0133  The Community Council of Nashua, NH / Greater Nashua 
Mental Health (Owner / Applicant) requesting site plan 
approval for a 3-story medical office building, with 
associated site improvements. Property is located at 44 
Simon Street. Map E – Lot 2247. Zoned Park Industrial 
(PI). Ward 4. 
Mr. Bollinger and Mr. LeClair recused from this case. Mr. Varley 
took place as Acting Chair. Voting members are Varley, Green 
Morgan, Hudson, and MacIntyre. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green that the application is complete and the 
Planning Board is ready to take jurisdiction 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Hudson 
 
MOTION CARRIED 5-0 
 
Jim Petropulos, Civil Engineer, IMEG Corp, 3 Congress St, Nashua 
NH
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 11 
 
 
Mr. Petropulos introduced himself on behalf of the owner. With him 
is Chief Operating Officer Maureen Ryan from Greater Nashua Mental 
Health. 
 
Mr. Petropulos said we are seeking site plan approval for a 
proposed medical office. He described the subject lot and 
surrounding properties. This parcel was once part of a larger lot 
to the north, Teradyne, and was primarily used for parking. In 
2017 the building was downsized and this lot was subdivided. In 
2023 we appeared here for an industrial flex building, that did 
not move forward. Greater Nashua Mental Health is a non-profit 
state designated community health center that serves Nashua and 9 
surrounding communities. The goal is to consolidate some of their 
facilities to this site.  
 
Mr. Petropulos briefly described site access, topography, and 
utilities. There is a city sewer line and a water line that pass 
through the site out towards the canal. What is being proposed is 
to redevelop the site to a 3-story, 98,000-sqft building. The 
building will contain admin offices, employee cubicles, common 
areas, waiting rooms, and treatment rooms. There are no overnight 
patients, this is outpatient only. There will be 300 employees, 
and typically 200 visitors per day. The hours are 8AM-6PM.  
 
Mr. Petropulos said are keeping two curb cuts off of Simon Street. 
We are proposing 400 parking spaces around the office. Open space 
will be increased to 33%. There are a couple of outdoor amenities, 
and we are proposing a connection to Mine Falls Park.  
 
Mr. Petropulos outlined stormwater improvements, traffic, 
landscaping, and architecture. They are asking for two waivers, as 
detailed in the staff report. The hope is to start construction 
this fall. The conditions outlined in the staff report are 
acceptable to the applicant.  
 
Mr. Varley asked if there are any other meaningful conditions or 
approvals they need beyond this one. Is there a capital campaign? 
 
Mr. Petropulos said there are state permits, he thinks they will 
be successful. Losing the Amherst Street site to the gas explosion 
has put a crimp in operations. They are very interested in moving 
forward.
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 12 
 
Ald. Morgan said UPS would share this intersection. Their peak 
hours are in the morning, about 8:30AM, and 4-6PM. Has there been 
any conversations with them? 
 
Mr. Durfee said staff has had conversations with UPS. 
 
Ald. Morgan asked if it would be addressed in the traffic study.  
 
Mr. Petropulos said we have not talked to UPS, nor would be need 
to. Our traffic consultant counted cars at Ledge Street, Simon 
Street, the highway exit, and West Hollis Street. UPS traffic would 
be baked into it. They crunched the numbers and concluded that 
there was adequate capacity at those intersections. 
 
Mr. Hudson said he would echo what was stated. And this could be 
symbiotic, the UPS trucks leaving as people start coming in.  
 
Ald. Morgan asked why one of the comments lists 250 vehicles per 
hour.  
 
Mr. Petropulos said that is during the peak hour. It’s not 250 
cars every hour. 
 
Mr. MacIntyre asked if the waiver requests meet the Master Plan. 
 
Mr. Muise said these are fairly common waiver requests. This isn’t 
on a major driven thoroughfare. Staff is confident in its 
recommendation. 
 
Mr. Petropulos said the 2007 code was written for retail buildings, 
and at the last minute they applied it to every building. You can’t 
ask for three planes of pitched roof on a medical building that 
has a flat roof. That forces us to ask for particular waivers.  
 
Mr. Durfee said under the new code what has been proposed would be 
compliant. The new code is more reflective of the Master Plan than 
the current code.  
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR CONCERN 
 
None 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR 
 
None
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 13 
 
Mr. MacIntyre thanked the applicant. He believes this will rid the 
city of one of the ugliest parking lots in the city. 
 
PUBLIC MEETING 
 
Mr. Varley closed the public hearing and opened the public meeting. 
He agreed with Mr. MacIntyre, he thinks this is a substantial 
improvement to the site. This applicant serves a critical role for 
the greater community. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve the following waivers for New 
Business – Site Plan A26-0133: 
 
a. §190-279 (EE): To waive the requirement to show existing 
conditions on ‘adjacent parcels as appropriate.  
 
b. b. §190-172: To waive certain architectural requirements for 
non-residential buildings. 
 
As per RSA 674:36(II)(N), RSA 674:44(III)(e), and §190-148(D), 
Strict conformity would pose an unnecessary hardship to the 
Applicant and the waiver would not be contrary to the spirit and 
intent of the regulations; and specific circumstances, or 
conditions of the land, and the waiver will properly carry out the 
spirit and intent of the regulations. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. MacIntyre 
 
MOTION CARRIED 5-0 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve New Business – Site Plan A26-0133. 
The Board finds that the application meets the Approval Criteria 
under §190-146(D) with the following conditions: 
 
a. Any waiver(s) granted shall be listed on the plan. Should any 
waiver(s) be denied, the plan must be revised in order to comply 
with the applicable site plan regulations.  
 
b. All outstanding comments from the Engineering Department, shall 
be addressed to the satisfaction of the Division of Public 
Works.  
 
c. Prior to the recording of the final plan, all technical review 
comments listed in Section 5 of the Planning Board staff report 
shall be addressed to the satisfaction of the Planning 
Department.
NCPB 
August 6, 2026 
Page 14 
 
 
d. The plan shall include a signature and seal of a New Hampshire 
licensed engineer, surveyor, and architect, on applicable 
sheets.  
 
e. Prior to any work being done, a pre-construction meeting with 
the City shall take place.  
 
f. Prior to any work being done, a financial guarantee for all off-
site improvements shall be approved and submitted to the City.  
 
g. Prior to the issuance of a building permit, stormwater documents

h. Prior to the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy, all site

k. All proposed demolition activities require inspections for the

l. Food or beverages sold or distributed at this location will be 
subject to licensure by the Environmental Health Department, 
and any supporting structures must be constructed according to 
He-P 2300. All such plans must be approved by the Environmental 
Health Department prior to construction.
NCPB 
August 6, 2026
